what_it_is: The discipline of working from the world as it is right now, not as it was when you last looked. The tip is the newest commit on main. Freshness is a two-leg check: (1) age - the input is young enough, and (2) tip identity - the tip SHA pinned in the input still equals the live tip, checked in the same step you act.
what_it_does: Prevents execution on moved ground. A tip move between generation and use invalidates every tip-pinned premise in a directive. The tip-match leg catches what the age bound cannot.
why_it_matters: A worker executed against a directive that was young but pinned to a dead tip: age said 'fresh', the tip said 'moved'. Without the tip-match leg, every gate downstream - scorecards, merges, verifications - would have been evaluated against ground that no longer existed. Stale bytes produce confident wrong answers.
key_rules: A directive is fresh only if BOTH legs pass: younger than its freshness bound (briefing: <45 min) AND pinned tip SHA == live tip. Age is necessary, never sufficient.

Tip-match in the same step you act: re-fetch the live ref (GET /repos/.../git/refs/heads/main - the ref, never the commits list endpoint, which can serve a stale cached commit) immediately before the action, not a step earlier.
Re-derive at action time: inputs come from live sources in the step where they are used. Never inherit state across steps (L12 re-fetch race clause: same step, no gap).
Declare DEGRADED honestly: if either leg fails, say so out loud (venue + record) and operate from live sources directly. A degraded directive is not a dead run (L398).
Tail reads follow the deconfliction rule: 100-per-page tail, page count re-verified on every fetch. Never per_page=1&page=N (returns the Nth-oldest, not the newest).
Proofs expire (Law 12): when the world moves, re-prove. A verdict anchored to a moved tip is history, not evidence.
The two legs apply to every live pointer, not just directives: mission-state branch, PR heads, check runs, venue tails.

not_covered: Proving the bytes are what they claim (independent seats, sabotage batteries, byte-identity)
Generating the directive (ranked batches, waves, directive construction)
Deep git mechanics beyond the ref-anchor procedure

mechanically_enforced: Directive orientation step zero (briefing section 0): directives must be <45 min old AND tip-matched, or the run declares DEGRADED and works from live sources. Fired in production.
L398 tip-match leg on every freshness check (standing law since 2026-10-14).
Deconfliction re-fetch rule: 100-per-page tail, page count re-verified every fetch.
TOOLS.md tip-anchoring rule: the ref is the authority; the commits list endpoint is advisory (from a real stale-serve incident 2026-10-09).
Law 12: proofs expire when the world changes.
proposed: A mechanical tip-match gate that refuses dispatch on a tip-mismatched directive instead of relying on the worker's own check. Today the worker catches it; tomorrow the gate should refuse it.

self_test: Does my pinned tip SHA match the live ref - right now, in this step?
Did I derive every input in THIS step, or inherit any from an earlier one?
If a leg failed, did I declare it and switch to live sources - or quietly proceed?
